title: Customer workload fingerprinting and SLA mapping for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Lina Ortega
description: Goal: produce a repeatable intake and triage flow that converts a customer's production workload signals into a recommended Dedicated capacity contract (reserved throughput, GPU class, autoscaling policy, and SLO targets). This ticket delivers: 1) a lightweight workload fingerprint spec and automated collector (script + one-click customer sample), 2) an SLA mapping table that ties fingerprint features to recommended reserved throughput and GPU class, 3) negotiation guidance and cost delta estimates, and 4) sample playbooks for canary, burst, and failure-mode handling. This is non-bug product work for enterprise intake — intended to reduce time-to-contract and improve SLA accuracy while reducing surprise overprovisioning.
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint spec defined with required fields: steady_qps, peak_qps, p50/p95/p99 latency at 512/1024 token lengths, avg token length, prefix-reuse rate, percent streaming, embedding/recall ratio, KV cache hit rate, typical batch size, model family and sequence-length sensitivity.
Automated collector prototype (Python script) that ingests 24h request logs and emits fingerprint JSON and a short summary PDF.
SLA mapping table that maps 10 canonical fingerprints to recommended (GPU class, reserved_throughput_tps, burst_policy, recommended_slo_99ms/p99/availability).
Cost delta estimator: given customer's fingerprint and chosen plan, returns monthly cost range and recommended trade-offs (e.g., reduce latency SLO or accept burst credits).
Playbook snippets for sales/solutions: onboarding checklist, preflight test plan (5k sample requests), and fallback route plan (model tiering + region fallback).
Stakeholder sign-off: Eng (Miguel Rios), Solutions (Priya Anand), Sales Engineer (Tomoko Sato) approve the mapping and collector outputs in review meeting.
Two pilot customers (internal staging customers allowed) complete the collector and receive a recommended dedicated proposal; feedback captured.
Confluence PRD and one demo notebook linked from this ticket.
Updated intake form in Console to include clear fingerprint upload or agent install instructions.
decision_log: 2026-02-18 | Lina Ortega: Use 99th percentile latency as the primary SLO metric for enterprise proposals; 95th and p50 included as advisory metrics.

2026-02-22 | Elliot Zhang: Default GPU recommendation uses empirical per-GPU throughput simulation rather than vendor nominal FLOPS; baseline supported GPUs: H100, A100, L4-equivalent for low-memory models.
2026-02-25 | Miguel Rios (Eng): Autoscale should be a hybrid: reserved baseline + burst credits (burst multiplier default 1.5) with queue-length-triggered prewarm at 70% GPU utilization.
2026-03-01 | Priya Anand (Solutions): For negotiations, present three options (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) showing cost vs SLO trade-offs; prefer Balanced by default.
2026-03-01 | Security: no additional security review required for collector (collector reads non-sensitive telemetry only); record maintained in Confluence.
2026-03-02 | Team consensus: Use sample-based simulation (1h replay) to estimate token-per-second and KV cache hit impact on throughput rather than purely analytic heuristics.
